title: The Dishonest Manager and the Rich Man and Lazarus

questions.question: In the Parable of the Dishonest Manager, what charge was brought to the rich man against his manager?
options: That this man was wasting his possessions
That he was stealing gold from the treasury secretly
That he had murdered a servant in anger
That he sold his master to the Romans
questions.correctAnswer: That this man was wasting his possessions
questions.explanation: Luke 16:1 (ESV): "He also said to the disciples, 'There was a rich man who had a manager, and charges were brought to him that this man was wasting his possessions.'"

questions.question: When the dishonest manager realized he was about to lose his position, what did he decide to do to ensure people would welcome him into their houses?
options: Summon his master's debtors and reduce their debts by altering their bills
Steal five bags of silver and bury them in a field
Run away to Egypt before he was caught
Beg the master for mercy and borrow money from his friends
questions.correctAnswer: Summon his master's debtors and reduce their debts by altering their bills
questions.explanation: Luke 16:4-5 (ESV): "I have decided what to do, so that when I am removed from management, people may receive me into their houses. So, summoning his master's debtors one by one..."

questions.question: How did the rich master react when he learned what the dishonest manager had done?
options: He commended the dishonest manager for his shrewdness
He sent the Roman guards to arrest him
He increased the debtors' bills twofold as a penalty
He beat the manager in the public square
questions.correctAnswer: He commended the dishonest manager for his shrewdness
questions.explanation: Luke 16:8 (ESV): "The master commended the dishonest manager for his shrewdness. For the sons of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light."

questions.question: Jesus teaches that "One who is faithful in a very little is..." what?
options: "...also faithful in much, and one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much."
"...given all the wealth of the master in time."
"...worthy of the kingdom of God."
"...given ten cities to rule over."
questions.correctAnswer: "...also faithful in much, and one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much."
questions.explanation: Luke 16:10 (ESV): "One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much, and one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much."

questions.question: Jesus states that "No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other." What two masters did He explicitly name?
options: God and money
Satan and Christ
Caesar and the Temple
The Law and Grace
questions.explanation: Luke 16:13 (ESV): "No servant can serve two masters... You cannot serve God and money."

questions.question: Who heard all these things regarding money and ridiculed Jesus?
options: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money
The Sadducees, who ruled the temple
The Herodians holding tax positions
The scribes writing new laws
questions.correctAnswer: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money
questions.explanation: Luke 16:14 (ESV): "The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things, and they ridiculed him."

questions.question: Jesus told the Pharisees: "You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts." Why? What is exalted among men?
options: It is an abomination in the sight of God
It is nothing but breath in the wind
It is celebrated but turns to dust
It brings false temporary peace
questions.correctAnswer: It is an abomination in the sight of God
questions.explanation: Luke 16:15 (ESV): "For what is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God."

questions.question: Jesus stated that it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for what to become void?
options: One dot of the Law
The temple in Jerusalem
The love of the Father
A single prophetic word of judgment
questions.explanation: Luke 16:17 (ESV): "But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one dot of the Law to become void."

questions.question: In the story of the rich man and Lazarus, where was the poor man covered with sores laid?
options: At his gate, desiring to be fed with what fell from the rich man's table
Outside the synagogue walls where dogs roamed
In the gutters of Jerusalem freezing in the cold
At the base of the Mount of Olives near a cave
questions.correctAnswer: At his gate, desiring to be fed with what fell from the rich man's table
questions.explanation: Luke 16:20-21 (ESV): "And at his gate was laid a poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores, who desired to be fed with what fell from the rich man's table."

questions.question: What happened when the poor man, Lazarus, died?
options: He was carried by the angels to Abraham's side
He was given a golden cup to drink pure water
He received his sight and was made king immediately
He was immediately resurrected to live forever on earth
questions.correctAnswer: He was carried by the angels to Abraham's side
questions.explanation: Luke 16:22 (ESV): "The poor man died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's side. The rich man also died and was buried,"

questions.question: In Hades, being in torment, what did the rich man see far off?
options: Abraham and Lazarus at his side
A great lake of fire swallowing all his wealth
The gates of heaven tightly shut
Legions of demons mocking his former glory
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham and Lazarus at his side
questions.explanation: Luke 16:23 (ESV): "and in Hades, being in torment, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham far off and Lazarus at his side."

questions.question: What did the rich man beg Abraham to send Lazarus to do for him?
options: Dip the end of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in anguish in this flame
Bring him a slice of bread from the heavenly banquet
Rescue him across the terrible chasm
Hide him from the piercing eyes of the judge
questions.correctAnswer: Dip the end of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in anguish in this flame
questions.explanation: Luke 16:24 (ESV): "...Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the end of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in anguish in this flame.'"

questions.question: Why did Abraham say Lazarus could not cross over to help the rich man?
options: Because between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, in order that those who would pass from here to you may not be able
Because the angels hold flaming swords to prevent it
Because the water of life evaporates instantly in hell
Because Lazarus must rest securely before the final day
questions.correctAnswer: Because between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, in order that those who would pass from here to you may not be able
questions.explanation: Luke 16:26 (ESV): "And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, in order that those who would pass from here to you may not be able, and none may cross from there to us."

questions.question: The rich man then asked Abraham to send Lazarus to his father's house to warn his how many brothers?
options: Five brothers
Three brothers
Seven brothers
Twelve brothers
questions.explanation: Luke 16:27-28 (ESV): "And he said, 'Then I beg you, father, to send him to my father's house—for I have five brothers—so that he may warn them...'"

questions.question: Abraham said the brothers had Moses and the Prophets to hear. What was Abraham's final reply when the rich man pleaded, "No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent"?
options: "If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be convinced if someone should rise from the dead."
"The dead cannot speak to the living, it is forbidden."
"Only a miracle of fire descending will convince them now."
"They are already condemned; the warning is too late."
questions.correctAnswer: "If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be convinced if someone should rise from the dead."
questions.explanation: Luke 16:31 (ESV): "He said to him, 'If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be convinced if someone should rise from the dead.'"

key_verse_text: "No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and money."
